passages.text: In the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, write down today’s date, for on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
This happened in the ninth year.
It was the tenth day of the tenth month.
The LORD said these words to me.
He called me “Son of man.”
He told me to write down today’s date.
He said, “Write the exact day.”
On this very day, the king of Babylon has attacked Jerusalem.
He has begun to lay siege to the city.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַתְּשִׁיעִית֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֥וֹר לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם כְּתוֹב לְךָ֙ אֶת־ שֵׁ֣ם הַיּ֔וֹם אֶת־ עֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה סָמַ֤ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶל֙ אֶל־ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Now speak a parable to this rebellious house and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Put the pot on the fire; put it on and pour in the water.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called the people of Israel a rebellious house.
God told Ezekiel to speak a parable to them.
God said, “This is what the Lord GOD says.
Put a pot on the fire.
Set the pot in place.
Pour water into the pot.”
passages.original: וּמְשֹׁ֤ל אֶל־ בֵּית־ הַמֶּ֙רִי֙ מָשָׁ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה שְׁפֹ֤ת הַסִּיר֙ שְׁפֹ֔ת וְגַם־ יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Put in the pieces of meat, every good piece— thigh and shoulder— fill it with choice bones.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God told Ezekiel to use a parable.
God told Ezekiel to speak to the rebellious people of Jerusalem.
God said, “Put the pieces of meat into the pot.
Put in every good piece.
Put in the thigh.
Put in the shoulder.
Fill the pot with the best bones.”
passages.original: אֱסֹ֤ף נְתָחֶ֙יהָ֙ אֵלֶ֔יהָ כָּל־ נֵ֥תַח ט֖וֹב יָרֵ֣ךְ וְכָתֵ֑ף מִבְחַ֥ר עֲצָמִ֖ים מַלֵּֽא׃

passages.text: Take the choicest of the flock and pile the fuel beneath it. Bring it to a boil and cook the bones in it.’
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to the rebellious house.
He gives a parable about judgment.
Take the best animals from the flock.
Place them in the pot.
Pile wood or fuel under the pot.
Make the fire strong.
Boil the contents of the pot.
Cook the bones inside the pot.
passages.original: מִבְחַ֤ר הַצֹּאן֙ לָק֔וֹחַ וְגַ֛ם דּ֥וּר הָעֲצָמִ֖ים תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ רַתַּ֣ח רְתָחֶ֔יהָ גַּם־ בָּשְׁל֥וּ עֲצָמֶ֖יהָ בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Woe to the city of bloodshed, to the pot now rusted, whose rust will not come off! Empty it piece by piece; cast no lots for its contents.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says, “Woe to the city of bloodshed.
This city is full of violence and murder.
This city is like a pot covered in rust.
The rust will not come off the pot.
Take out the pieces from the pot, one by one.
Do not cast lots for the pieces.
Remove everything from the pot, piece by piece.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־ אָמַ֣ר׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה אוֹי֮ עִ֣יר הַדָּמִים֒ סִ֚יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֶלְאָתָ֣ה בָ֔הּ וְחֶ֨לְאָתָ֔הּ לֹ֥א יָצְאָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נָּה לִנְתָחֶ֤יהָ לִנְתָחֶ֙יהָ֙ הוֹצִיאָ֔הּ לֹא־ נָפַ֥ל עָלֶ֖יהָ גּוֹרָֽל׃

passages.text: For the blood she shed is still within her; she poured it out on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust.
passages.sermon:
The city is guilty of bloodshed.
Her blood remains inside her.
She poured her blood on a bare rock.
She did not pour her blood on the ground.
She did not cover her blood with dust.
passages.original: כִּ֤י דָמָהּ֙ בְּתוֹכָ֣הּ הָיָ֔ה עַל־ צְחִ֥יחַ סֶ֖לַע שָׂמָ֑תְהוּ לֹ֤א שְׁפָכַ֙תְהוּ֙ עַל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ לְכַסּ֥וֹת עָלָ֖יו עָפָֽר׃

passages.text: In order to stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have placed her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks with authority.
God wants to stir up anger.
God wants to take vengeance.
God has placed her blood on the bare rock.
God does not allow the blood to be covered.
passages.original: לְהַעֲל֤וֹת חֵמָה֙ לִנְקֹ֣ם נָקָ֔ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־ דָּמָ֖הּ עַל־ צְחִ֣יחַ סָ֑לַע לְבִלְתִּ֖י הִכָּסֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: Yes, this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Woe to the city of bloodshed! I, too, will pile the kindling high.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He is the subject.
He is powerful and just.
He says, “Woe to the city of bloodshed.”
This city is violent.
This city is guilty of shedding blood.
The Lord will act against it.
He will pile the kindling high.
He will prepare for judgment.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה א֖וֹי עִ֣יר הַדָּמִ֑ים גַּם־ אֲנִ֖י אַגְדִּ֥יל הַמְּדוּרָֽה׃

passages.text: Pile on the logs and kindle the fire; cook the meat well and mix in the spices; let the bones be burned.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the city of bloodshed.
He commands action.
Add many logs to the fire.
Light the fire strongly.
Cook the meat until it is done.
Mix in the spices.
Burn the bones completely.
passages.original: הַרְבֵּ֤ה הָעֵצִים֙ הַדְלֵ֣ק הָאֵ֔שׁ הָתֵ֖ם הַבָּשָׂ֑ר וְהַרְקַח֙ הַמֶּרְקָחָ֔ה וְהָעֲצָמ֖וֹת יֵחָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Set the empty pot on its coals until it becomes hot and its copper glows. Then its impurity will melt within; its rust will be consumed.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to the city of bloodshed.
He commands to set the empty pot on its coals.
The pot must be empty.
Place it directly on the coals.
Wait until the pot becomes hot.
Wait until its copper glows.
The impurity inside the pot will melt.
The rust inside the pot will be consumed.
passages.original: וְהַעֲמִידֶ֥הָ עַל־ גֶּחָלֶ֖יהָ רֵקָ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן תֵּחַ֜ם וְחָ֣רָה נְחֻשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְנִתְּכָ֤ה בְתוֹכָהּ֙ טֻמְאָתָ֔הּ תִּתֻּ֖ם חֶלְאָתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: It has frustrated every effort; its thick rust has not been removed, even by the fire.
passages.sermon:
The pot has thick rust.
The rust frustrates every effort to remove it.
The fire cannot remove the rust.
The rust remains, even after burning.
passages.original: תְּאֻנִ֖ים הֶלְאָ֑ת וְלֹֽא־ תֵצֵ֤א מִמֶּ֙נָּה֙ רַבַּ֣ת חֶלְאָתָ֔הּ בְּאֵ֖שׁ חֶלְאָתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Because of the indecency of your uncleanness I tried to cleanse you, but you would not be purified from your filthiness. You will not be pure again until My wrath against you has subsided.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
Israel is unclean.
Israel’s uncleanness is indecent.
God tried to cleanse Israel.
Israel did not become pure.
Israel refused to be purified from its filthiness.
Israel will not be pure again.
Israel will remain unclean until God’s wrath is finished.
passages.original: בְּטֻמְאָתֵ֖ךְ זִמָּ֑ה יַ֤עַן טִֽהַרְתִּיךְ֙ וְלֹ֣א טָהַ֔רְתְּ מִטֻּמְאָתֵךְ֙ לֹ֣א תִטְהֲרִי־ ע֔וֹד עַד־ הֲנִיחִ֥י אֶת־ חֲמָתִ֖י בָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: I, the LORD, have spoken; the time is coming, and I will act. I will not refrain or show pity, nor will I relent. I will judge you according to your ways and deeds,’ declares the Lord GOD.”
passages.sermon:
I am the LORD.
I have spoken.
The time is coming.
I will act.
I will not hold back.
I will not show pity.
I will not relent.
I will judge you.
I will judge you by your ways.
I will judge you by your deeds.
This is what the Lord GOD declares.
passages.original: אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה דִּבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ בָּאָ֣ה וְעָשִׂ֔יתִי לֹֽא־ אֶפְרַ֥ע וְלֹא־ אָח֖וּס וְלֹ֣א אֶנָּחֵ֑ם כִּדְרָכַ֤יִךְ וְכַעֲלִילוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ שְׁפָט֔וּךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, behold, I am about to take away the desire of your eyes with a fatal blow. But you must not mourn or weep or let your tears flow.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He said these words to me.
He called me “son of man.”
He told me what would happen.
He said, “I am about to take away the desire of your eyes.”
He meant my wife, whom I loved.
He said she would die by a sudden blow.
He commanded me not to mourn for her.
He told me not to weep.
He told me not to let my tears fall.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם הִנְנִ֨י לֹקֵ֧חַ מִמְּךָ֛ אֶת־ מַחְמַ֥ד עֵינֶ֖יךָ בְּמַגֵּפָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִסְפֹּד֙ וְלֹ֣א תִבְכֶּ֔ה וְל֥וֹא תָב֖וֹא דִּמְעָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Groan quietly; do not mourn for the dead. Put on your turban and strap your sandals on your feet; do not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Ezekiel.
The LORD gave Ezekiel a command.
Ezekiel must groan quietly.
Ezekiel must not mourn for the dead.
Ezekiel must not show public grief.
Ezekiel must put on his turban.
Ezekiel must wear his sandals on his feet.
Ezekiel must not cover his lips.
Ezekiel must not eat the bread of mourners.
passages.original: הֵאָנֵ֣ק׀ דֹּ֗ם מֵתִים֙ אֵ֣בֶל לֹֽא־ תַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה פְאֵֽרְךָ֙ חֲב֣וֹשׁ עָלֶ֔יךָ וּנְעָלֶ֖יךָ תָּשִׂ֣ים בְּרַגְלֶ֑יךָ וְלֹ֤א תַעְטֶה֙ עַל־ שָׂפָ֔ם וְלֶ֥חֶם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל׃

passages.text: So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died. And the next morning I did as I had been commanded.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet of God.
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God told Ezekiel that his wife would die.
Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning.
In the evening, Ezekiel’s wife died.
The next morning, Ezekiel obeyed God’s command.
passages.original: וָאֲדַבֵּ֤ר אֶל־ הָעָם֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֥מָת אִשְׁתִּ֖י בָּעָ֑רֶב וָאַ֥עַשׂ בַּבֹּ֖קֶר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צֻוֵּֽיתִי׃

passages.text: Then the people asked me, “Won’t you tell us what these things you are doing mean to us?”
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to me.
They asked me a question.
They said, “Will you not tell us what these actions mean for us?”
They wanted to know the meaning of what I was doing.
They saw my actions and wanted an explanation.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלַ֖י הָעָ֑ם הֲלֹֽא־ תַגִּ֥יד לָ֙נוּ֙ מָה־ אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֔נוּ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: So I answered them, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying: Tell the house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I am about to desecrate My sanctuary, the pride of your power, the desire of your eyes, and the delight of your soul. And the sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword.’
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet of God.
The people asked Ezekiel about his actions.
Ezekiel answered the people.
Ezekiel said, “The word of the LORD came to me.
God spoke to me.
God told me to speak to the house of Israel.
God said, ‘I am the Lord GOD.
I will desecrate My sanctuary.
My sanctuary is the pride of your power.
My sanctuary is the desire of your eyes.
My sanctuary is the delight of your soul.
Your sons and daughters, whom you left behind, will fall by the sword.’”
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם דְּבַ֨ר־ יְהוָ֔ה הָיָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃ אֱמֹ֣ר׀ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּֽה־ אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנְנִ֨י מְחַלֵּ֤ל אֶת־ מִקְדָּשִׁי֙ גְּא֣וֹן עֻזְּכֶ֔ם מַחְמַ֥ד עֵֽינֵיכֶ֖ם וּמַחְמַ֣ל נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וּבְנֵיכֶ֧ם וּבְנֽוֹתֵיכֶ֛ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲזַבְתֶּ֖ם בַּחֶ֥רֶב יִפֹּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Then you will do as I have done: You will not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God told Ezekiel to speak to Israel.
God said Israel would act as Ezekiel acted.
You will do what I have done.
You will not cover your lips.
You will not eat the bread of mourners.
passages.original: וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי עַל־ שָׂפָם֙ לֹ֣א תַעְט֔וּ וְלֶ֥חֶם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your sins, and you will groan among yourselves.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel through Ezekiel.
God told them what would happen when He judged them for their sins.
Your turbans will stay on your heads.
Your sandals will stay on your feet.
You will not mourn.
You will not weep.
You will waste away because of your sins.
You will groan to one another.
passages.original: וּפְאֵרֵכֶ֣ם עַל־ רָאשֵׁיכֶ֗ם וְנַֽעֲלֵיכֶם֙ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תִסְפְּד֖וּ וְלֹ֣א תִבְכּ֑וּ וּנְמַקֹּתֶם֙ בַּעֲוֺנֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וּנְהַמְתֶּ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־ אָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: ‘Thus Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do everything that he has done. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.’
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel is a prophet of God.
God made Ezekiel a sign for the people.
You will do everything Ezekiel has done.
You will follow his actions exactly.
When these things happen, you will know something important.
You will know that I am the Lord GOD.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה יְחֶזְקֵ֤אל לָכֶם֙ לְמוֹפֵ֔ת כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ בְּבֹאָ֕הּ וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס

passages.text: And you, son of man, know that on the day I take away their stronghold, their pride and joy—the desire of their eyes which uplifted their souls—and their sons and daughters as well, on that day a fugitive will come and tell you the news.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel, the son of man.
God said He would take away the stronghold of the people of Israel.
God would remove what they took pride in and what brought them joy.
God would take away what was precious to their eyes.
God would remove what their souls longed for.
God would take away their sons and their daughters.
On that same day, a fugitive would come to Ezekiel.
The fugitive would bring news to Ezekiel’s ears.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֔ם הֲל֗וֹא בְּי֨וֹם קַחְתִּ֤י מֵהֶם֙ אֶת־ מָ֣עוּזָּ֔ם מְשׂ֖וֹשׂ תִּפְאַרְתָּ֑ם אֶת־ מַחְמַ֤ד עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת־ מַשָּׂ֣א נַפְשָׁ֔ם בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְנוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יָב֥וֹא הַפָּלִ֖יט אֵלֶ֑יךָ לְהַשְׁמָע֖וּת אָזְנָֽיִם׃

passages.text: On that day your mouth will be opened to him who has escaped; you will speak and no longer be mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God told Ezekiel about a future day.
On that day, a fugitive will come to Ezekiel.
God will open Ezekiel’s mouth to speak to the fugitive.
Ezekiel will no longer be silent.
Ezekiel will become a sign to the people.
The people will know that God is the LORD.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִפָּ֤תַח פִּ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ הַפָּלִ֔יט וּתְדַבֵּ֕ר וְלֹ֥א תֵֽאָלֵ֖ם ע֑וֹד וְהָיִ֤יתָ לָהֶם֙ לְמוֹפֵ֔ת וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
